newsitem.title: MACAU: Air Macau operating loss $7.5 mln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Air Macau operating loss $7.5 mln in 1996.

text.p: Air Macau Co Ltd, the flag carrier of the Portuguese-run enclave bordering southern China, said on Thursday it posted an operating loss of about 60 million patacas (US$7.5 million) in 1996, its first full year of operation.
The loss was about half the initial forecast, an airline spokesman said. Turnover was 650 million patacas.
The company's assets were valued at about 500 million patacas, the spokesman said.
Air Macau said it carried 665,000 passengers on 5,700 flights last year, and had an average occupancy rate of 68 percent.

The airline plans to start service three times a week to northeast China's Qingdao city on March 23 after taking delivery of its fifth Airbus Industrie aircraft in late February. Its sixth Airbus is scheduled to be delivered in May.
Its entire start-up fleet of Airbus Industrie aircraft has been leased from U.S.-based International Lease Finance Corp.
Air Macau said it would be flying two 150-seat A-320s and four 178-seat A-321s by May.
Air Macau, 51 percent held by Chinese airline Air China, flies to Beijing, Shanghai, Xiamen, Bangkok, Taipei and Kaohsiung.

Other major stakeholders include TAP-Air Portugal in conjunction with Portuguese Banco Comercial de Macau and Banco Nacional Ultramarino with 25 percent, Stanley Ho's casino monopoly company STDM with 14 percent and the Macau government with five percent.
Air Macau began operations on November 9, 1995.
